evidence.snippet:
These LCRs mediate meiotic non-
allelic homologous recombination and are susceptible to
either deletion or duplication of these intervals.
evidence.explanation: This supports the recurrent LCR-mediated deletion mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The typical 3 Mb LCR22 A-D deletion was present in 2,788 individuals (92.4%), with smaller A-B (n=172, 5.7%) and A-C (n=56, 1.9%) deletions comprising the remaining cohort.
evidence.explanation: A large contemporary cohort documents the dominant recurrent deletion and smaller proximal classes.

evidence.snippet: The review of the literature confirms the hypothesis that the 22q11.2DS phenotype results from a network of interactions between deleted protein-coding genes and altered epigenetic regulation.
evidence.explanation: This supports a multigene and regulatory-network model rather than singular TBX1 causation.

steps/1.description: Low-copy repeats at 22q11.2 predispose to non-allelic homologous recombination and recurrent deletions. The common A-D interval removes more than 40 coding genes, so the syndrome reflects combined dosage effects and background modifiers rather than a single-gene lesion.

evidence.snippet: An estimated 67–80% of individuals affected with 22q11.2del have some degree of T cell lymphopenia (TCL).
evidence.explanation: This establishes T-cell lymphopenia as the common immune presentation.

steps/2.description: Reduced thymic tissue can lower thymic T-cell output. Most immune phenotypes are milder T-cell lymphopenia rather than congenital athymia, and clinical appearance alone does not reliably identify the immune severity.

evidence.snippet: Ranbp1(-/-)-dependent proliferative deficits substantially diminish the frequency of layer 2/3, but not layer 5/6 cortical projection neurons.
evidence.explanation: Homozygous mouse knockout supports a candidate cortical mechanism but is not equivalent to human hemizygosity.

evidence.snippet: With regard to the SPEM performance, there was a significant interaction between the COMT158 genotype and proline level with significantly decreased SPEM performance in children with high plasma proline levels and the low activity COMTmet allele.
evidence.explanation: The small human study supports a limited genotype-by-metabolite association, not a general mechanism for psychosis.

steps/3.description: RANBP1-null mice show impaired upper-layer cortical neuron generation, and a small human study found a COMT-genotype-by-proline association with selected neurophysiologic measures. These observations are candidate mechanisms; they do not establish a causal path from an individual interval gene to human learning difficulties or schizophrenia.

evidence.snippet: Tbx1-/- mice displayed a wide range of developmental anomalies encompassing almost all of the common DGS/VCFS features, including hypoplasia of the thymus and parathyroid glands, cardiac outflow tract abnormalities, abnormal facial structures, abnormal vertebrae and cleft palate
evidence.explanation: Homozygous knockout supports developmental plausibility, but it is not dosage-equivalent to a heterozygous human multigene deletion.

steps/4.description: TBX1 dosage is an important contributor to pharyngeal-apparatus and cardiac outflow development. Heterozygous Tbx1 mice model aortic/outflow anomalies, whereas the broader phenotype occurs mainly after homozygous loss; those dosage differences limit extrapolation to the human multigene deletion.

evidence.snippet: Patients who underwent palatoplasty achieved an increase in velar length, but this did not lead to resolution of hypernasality, suggesting that underlying anatomical differences such as increased pharyngeal depth and hypodynamic muscles may make palatoplasty less effective at resolving hypernasality in patients with 22q.
evidence.explanation: Names both components of this node - pharyngeal depth (structural) and hypodynamic muscles (myogenic) - and shows they persist after velar lengthening, which is why the node is not reducible to palatal anatomy.

steps/5.description: The velopharyngeal port fails to close during speech because of combined structural and muscular factors - a deep pharynx, palatal anomalies that are often submucous rather than overt, and hypodynamic pharyngeal musculature. This is the mechanistic substrate of the historical velocardiofacial presentation, and it is the proposed explanation for resonance persisting after a purely palatal repair - proposed rather than established, since the supporting surgical comparison is a 14-patient series.

evidence.snippet: Typical miRNA expression patterns have been identified in 22q11.2DS, due to an alteration in miRNA biogenesis, affecting the expression of several target genes.
evidence.explanation: The review supports altered miRNA biogenesis while leaving phenotype-level causality unresolved.

steps/6.description: DGCR8 hemizygosity can perturb microRNA biogenesis and downstream gene regulation. This is a candidate contributor to variable expression, not a proven explanation for any single clinical feature.

evidence.snippet: The most frequent class of defects in 22q11.2DS are CTDs; they occurred in 40% of this cohort.
evidence.explanation: The 40% conotruncal-defect estimate supports the FREQUENT band.

evidence.snippet: congenital heart disease, particularly conotruncal malformations (ventricular septal defect, tetralogy of Fallot, interrupted aortic arch, and truncus arteriosus)
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews documents the characteristic lesion spectrum.

steps/7.description: Congenital heart disease is heterogeneous and often conotruncal, including tetralogy of Fallot, interrupted aortic arch, truncus arteriosus, and septal defects. A recent 3,016-person specialist-center cohort found congenital heart disease in 59% and conotruncal defects in 40%.

evidence.snippet: Patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DelS) often present with velopharyngeal dysfunction (VPD). VPD in patients with 22q11DelS is multifactorial beyond velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) alone, and differences in surgical outcomes are poorly understood.
evidence.explanation: States both that velopharyngeal dysfunction is a common presenting feature of the deletion syndrome and that it is multifactorial rather than reducible to velopharyngeal insufficiency alone.

evidence.snippet: 22q11.2DS presents a uniquely high burden of ENT disease across the lifespan, including chronic otitis media, elevated cholesteatoma risk, persistent velopharyngeal dysfunction, multilevel airway anomalies, sleep-disordered breathing, dysphagia, and perioperative vulnerability due to vascular, immunologic, and hematologic anomalies.
evidence.explanation: A 2026 otolaryngology state-of-the-art review lists persistent velopharyngeal dysfunction among the lifelong ENT burden of the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: While not all people with 22q have a palatal abnormality, up to 80% of people with 22q present with VPI.
evidence.explanation: Supports the FREQUENT band (30-79%). The figure is an upper bound, so it is not read as VERY_FREQUENT; the deep-research report's own phenotype table independently gives ~65-70% for the palatal group. Note this sentence is the paper's introductory summary of the literature rather than a result of its own 14-patient series.

steps/8.description: Failure of the velopharyngeal port to close during speech is the "velo" component of the historical velocardiofacial (Shprintzen) presentation. GeneReviews lists velopharyngeal incompetence alongside - rather than as a consequence of - submucous and overt cleft palate, so it is curated separately from the palatal structural anomalies above. Note that the literature treats velopharyngeal dysfunction in this syndrome as broader than velopharyngeal insufficiency alone; this phenotype is bound to the insufficiency term, and the additional contributors are modelled in the upstream mechanism node.

evidence.snippet: Resonance and speech sound disorders may also present and include hypernasality and compensatory misarticulation errors that require speech therapy.
evidence.explanation: Establishes hypernasality as part of the syndrome's speech phenotype at the population level. An earlier draft quoted the preoperative severity split of the same paper's surgical arm, but presence of hypernasality was an inclusion criterion of that study, so those proportions are true by construction and cannot evidence the phenotype.

steps/9.description: Hypernasal resonance is the audible speech consequence of the incompetent velopharyngeal port and is the feature that most often brings affected children to speech surgery. Its persistence after palatoplasty in this syndrome is attributed to pharyngeal anatomy and muscle tone rather than to a residual palatal cleft.

evidence.snippet: An estimated 67–80% of individuals affected with 22q11.2del have some degree of T cell lymphopenia (TCL).
evidence.explanation: The 67-80% estimate maps to the FREQUENT band.

steps/10.description: T-cell lymphopenia varies from mild laboratory reduction to clinically important immune dysfunction; immune severity cannot be inferred from external syndromic features alone.

evidence.explanation: The approximately 0.5% estimate maps to the VERY_RARE band.

steps/11.description: Congenital absence of thymus function causes profound T-cell deficiency in a small subset and requires specialized immune management.

edges/2.description: The recurrent proximal deletion makes TBX1 hemizygous.

edges/3.description: The recurrent proximal deletion makes DGCR8 hemizygous.

edges/4.description: Combined deleted-region dosage effects can impair thymic development, but individual-gene attribution and modifiers remain incompletely resolved.

edges/5.description: Deleted-region dosage creates several candidate neurodevelopmental mechanisms whose human causal contributions remain uncertain.

evidence.snippet: Tbx1-/- mice displayed a wide range of developmental anomalies encompassing almost all of the common DGS/VCFS features, including hypoplasia of the thymus and parathyroid glands, cardiac outflow tract abnormalities, abnormal facial structures, abnormal vertebrae and cleft palate
evidence.explanation: Cleft palate in the homozygous null links Tbx1-dependent pharyngeal development to the palatal arm of the phenotype. INDIRECT because the model is homozygous and murine, whereas the human lesion is a heterozygous multigene deletion.

evidence.snippet: Neural crest development is usually impacted leading to various cardiovascular defects including Tetralogy of Fallot and truncus arteriosus. It can also cause palatal defects, especially velopharyngeal deficiency
evidence.explanation: States the edge directly in human terms: the same pharyngeal neural-crest disruption that produces the conotruncal lesions also produces velopharyngeal deficiency. This is the human-level counterpart of the dosage-mismatched mouse evidence above.

edges/6.description: The same pharyngeal-apparatus vulnerability that underlies the outflow lesion also underlies the velopharyngeal and palatal phenotype. The mouse evidence is homozygous-null and so is dosage-mismatched to the human heterozygous deletion; it supports developmental plausibility rather than a direct human causal claim.

evidence.snippet: mice heterozygous for the mutation had a high incidence of cardiac outflow tract anomalies, thus modeling one of the major abnormalities of the human syndrome
evidence.explanation: Heterozygous mouse evidence supports a cardiac contribution but not the full human contiguous-gene syndrome.

edges/7.description: TBX1 dosage contributes to conotruncal and aortic-arch susceptibility, but other deleted genes and genome-wide modifiers also shape the human lesion.

evidence.snippet: Patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DelS) often present with velopharyngeal dysfunction (VPD). VPD in patients with 22q11DelS is multifactorial beyond velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) alone, and differences in surgical outcomes are poorly understood.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that velopharyngeal dysfunction in this syndrome is multifactorial rather than a simple palatal-closure defect.

evidence.snippet: People with 22q can have multiple anatomic/physiologic differences of the velopharynx that contribute to VPI. These differences may include palatal clefting, increased pharyngeal depth due to velopharyngeal disproportion, decreased velar thickness, thin levator veli palatini muscles, discontinuity of the levator veli palatini muscles, decreased velar length, and pharyngeal hypotonia.
evidence.explanation: States the edge directly: it names the anatomic and physiologic differences of the velopharynx that contribute to velopharyngeal insufficiency, which is exactly the content of the upstream node.

edges/8.description: Incomplete closure of the velopharyngeal port is the direct functional expression of this combined structural and myogenic deficit.

evidence.snippet: In patients with 22q, palatoplasty procedures may be less effective than pharyngoplasty procedures at resolving hypernasality. This may be due to underlying anatomic or physiologic differences, such as increased pharyngeal depth and hypodynamic muscles.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the hypernasality specifically to pharyngeal depth and hypodynamic muscles, which is the causal content of this edge rather than of either node alone.

edges/9.description: Air escape through the incompletely closed port produces hypernasal resonance, which resists palatoplasty in this syndrome because the pharyngeal and myogenic components are not addressed by palatal repair.

evidence.snippet: Thus, barring a specific T cell defect such as SCID, a normal thymic volume in 22q11.2del, results in a normal number of T cells, whereas a small thymus can result in a quantitative T cell deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The guideline directly links thymic size to quantitative T-cell deficiency.

edges/10.description: Reduced thymic tissue lowers T-cell output.

evidence.explanation: This identifies and quantifies congenital athymia specifically in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.

edges/11.description: Complete absence of thymic function is the rare severe end of the developmental defect.

evidence.snippet: The typical 3 Mb LCR22 A-D deletion was present in 2,788 individuals (92.4%), with smaller A-B (n=172, 5.7%) and A-C (n=56, 1.9%) deletions comprising the remaining cohort.
evidence.explanation: This large cohort quantifies the proximal recurrent deletion classes represented in the study.

evidence.snippet: too small to be visualized on standard G-banded karyotype analysis
evidence.explanation: This supports the limitation of routine karyotyping.

evidence.snippet: We identified three mutations of TBX1 in two unrelated patients without the 22q11.2 deletion-one with sporadic conotruncal anomaly face syndrome/velocardiofacial syndrome and one with sporadic DiGeorge's syndrome-and in three patients from a family with conotruncal anomaly face syndrome/velocardiofacial syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Human evidence that TBX1 point mutations without a 22q11.2 deletion reproduce the DiGeorge and velocardiofacial presentations. It is cited here because the only other support on this record is a mouse study, and a human phenotype should not rest on model-organism evidence alone.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that the TBX1 mutation is responsible for five major phenotypes in del22q11.2 syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion, quoted for the "major contributor" wording of this record's `association`. Marked INDIRECT because it is an inference the authors draw from five deletion-negative patients rather than a measurement of TBX1's contribution within the deletion.

evidence.snippet: we propose that TBX1 in humans is a key gene in the etiology of DGS/VCFS
evidence.explanation: The mouse study supports TBX1 as a key contributor, not as the sole cause of the human syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac anomalies affect 75–80% of individuals with 22q11.2del, and a significant number of these patients will require cardiac surgery at an early age.
evidence.explanation: The guideline directly supports early cardiac surgery for a substantial affected subset.

treatments/0.description: Congenital cardiac lesions require cardiology assessment and, for many severe lesions, surgery or catheter-based intervention in infancy.

evidence.snippet: calcium supplementation and referral to an endocrinologist and nephrologist because of increased risk of renal calculi if long-term supplementation is required
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews directly supports calcium replacement and specialist follow-up.

treatments/1.description: Treat documented hypocalcemia with calcium replacement and specialist endocrine follow-up; long-term supplementation requires monitoring for renal complications. This entry does not infer a universal calcitriol regimen.

evidence.snippet: The initial immunologic evaluation recommended at the time of diagnosis should include T (CD3, CD4, CD8), B (CD19 or CD20), and natural killer (CD16 or CD56) cell (TBNK) quantitation
evidence.explanation: The guideline specifies the initial immune evaluation.

evidence.snippet: live vaccine administration (MMR and varicella) in 22q11.2del
evidence.explanation: This identifies the guideline table as criteria for live MMR and varicella vaccination.

evidence.explanation: The table provides all four immune-function criteria for live-vaccine eligibility.

treatments/2.description: At diagnosis, assess T-, B-, and NK-cell numbers and naïve/memory T-cell subsets. Subsequent immunoglobulin, vaccine-response, and lymphocyte testing should be individualized. Live MMR and varicella vaccines require adequate immune-function criteria rather than a syndromic label alone.

evidence.snippet: Whenever possible, the diagnosis of congenital athymia should be determined prior to surgery, as this small subset of patients requires blood products that are irradiated, leukocyte reduced, and CMV negative.
evidence.explanation: The guideline directly supports the conditional blood-product precautions.

treatments/3.description: Use appropriately treated cellular blood products for congenital athymia or severe/suspected T-cell deficiency, including when immune evaluation cannot be completed before surgery.

evidence.snippet: Survival following implant was 72% (76 of the 105 patients).
evidence.explanation: The guideline summarizes outcomes from a 105-implant single-center series.

evidence.snippet: circulating naïve T cells were detectable by 6 months post-implantation [124, 125].
evidence.explanation: This supports a months-long immune-reconstitution timeline.

treatments/4.description: Cultured thymus tissue implantation is reserved for confirmed congenital athymia, not routine T-cell lymphopenia. Immune reconstitution takes months and specialized infection prophylaxis is required during that interval.

evidence.snippet: occupational, physical, and speech therapy with introduction of sign language by age one year, educational and behavioral therapy
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews supports multidisciplinary developmental and communication intervention.

treatments/5.description: Coordinate palate/ENT assessment, speech and language therapy, developmental and educational intervention, feeding support, and audiology or hearing aids according to the individual's findings.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, 86% of patients in the pharyngoplasty group had resolution of hypernasality.
evidence.explanation: Reports the pharyngoplasty resolution rate that motivates preferring it over palatoplasty in this syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Matched for age and pre-operative velopharyngeal closure, patients with and without 22q11DelS and VPI had similar benefits after sphincter pharyngoplasty.
evidence.explanation: A 134-patient matched cohort supports offering sphincter pharyngoplasty on the same terms as in non-syndromic velopharyngeal insufficiency.

treatments/6.description:
Speech surgery for velopharyngeal insufficiency that persists after speech therapy. A small single-centre series (14 patients, 7 per arm) reported that pharyngoplasty resolved hypernasality where palatoplasty did not, which the authors attributed to the deficit being pharyngeal and myogenic as well as palatal; the comparison is underpowered and is reported by its authors as a "may be less effective" signal rather than a settled preference. Separately, and in a larger matched cohort, outcomes after sphincter pharyngoplasty are comparable to those in non-syndromic patients, so the deletion is not by itself a reason to expect surgical failure.
NCIT has no pharyngoplasty or velopharyngeal-repair term reachable from NCIT:C25218, so the binding is the generic surgical action and the specificity is carried in preferred_term.

evidence.snippet: No patient who underwent palatoplasty achieved resolution of hypernasality; 1/7 patients had worse hypernasality, 4/7 had no change, and 2/7 had improved hypernasality.
evidence.explanation: The contrast between the two procedures is what ties the surgical target to the pharyngeal/myogenic mechanism rather than to the palate alone.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: Pharyngoplasty narrows the velopharyngeal port, addressing the pharyngeal and myogenic components of the node that palatal repair alone leaves.

evidence.snippet: These recommendations provide contemporary guidance for evaluation, surveillance, and management of the many 22q11.2DS-associated physical, cognitive, behavioral, and psychiatric morbidities while addressing important genetic counseling and psychosocial issues.
evidence.explanation: The updated pediatric recommendations support coordinated multidisciplinary follow-up.

evidence.snippet: These recommendations provide guidance for the recognition, evaluation, surveillance, and management of the many emerging and chronic 22q11.2DS-associated multisystem morbidities relevant to adults.
evidence.explanation: The updated adult recommendations support lifelong, multisystem surveillance.

treatments/7.description: Surveillance should be individualized across cardiology, immune function, calcium and thyroid status, blood counts, palate/feeding and ENT, hearing, vision, renal and skeletal findings, development, and psychiatric health, with planned transition from pediatric to adult care.

evidence.snippet: Offspring of affected individuals have a 50% chance of inheriting the 22q11.2 deletion.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews provides the key transmission-risk basis for counseling.

treatments/8.description: Offer parental testing, deletion-class-specific recurrence counseling, and reproductive counseling. An affected parent has a 50% transmission risk, but phenotype severity cannot be predicted prenatally.

evidence.snippet: These lesion-specific findings suggest the hypothesis that deletion interval and broader genetic background may contribute to CHD variability in 22q11.2DS, pending future replication.
evidence.explanation: The large human cohort identifies deletion interval and background variation as testable contributors while calling for replication.

open_questions/0.rationale: TBX1 is a major developmental contributor but does not explain the full contiguous-gene syndrome. A large cohort now links deletion size and background variation to lesion-specific cardiac outcomes, while overall genotype-phenotype prediction remains weak. Resolving gene- and tissue-specific contributions is necessary to avoid both singular-TBX1 attribution and untestable multigene narratives.

open_questions/1.rationale: Homozygous mouse knockouts reproduce striking developmental phenotypes but differ in gene dosage, deleted interval, species, and sometimes viability from affected humans. The COMT/proline observation is also a small, phenotype-specific association. Human isogenic models are needed before these findings are promoted to syndrome-wide causal pathways.

evidence.snippet: These features overlap with other neurodevelopmental conditions, including Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS), and may be incompletely penetrant or demonstrate variable expressivity, depending on the specific chromosomal anomaly.
evidence.explanation: The 103-person literature review supports incomplete penetrance and chromosome-anomaly-dependent expressivity.

evidence.snippet: loss of HDAC4 function usually occurs as part of larger deletions of chromosome 2q37; BDMR is also known as chromosome 2q37 deletion syndrome, and the precise role of HDAC4 within the phenotype remains uncertain.
evidence.explanation: The authors explicitly place HDAC4 loss in the larger deletion context and identify uncertainty about its phenotype-specific contribution.

steps/1.description: Terminal and interstitial 2q37 deletions remove variable gene content and produce a contiguous-gene dosage disorder. Clinical expressivity is incomplete and depends on the specific chromosome anomaly; the available evidence does not support a simple rule that larger deletions always cause more severe disease.

evidence.snippet: sequencing of HDAC4 identified de novo mutations, including one intragenic deletion probably disrupting normal splicing and one intragenic insertion that results in a frameshift and premature stop codon.
evidence.explanation: Deletion-negative individuals with truncating HDAC4 variants support a gene-level contribution to an overlapping phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Presented here are three individuals with haploinsufficiency of HDAC4 who have brachydactyly type E, non-dysmorphic facial features, and normal intelligence.
evidence.explanation: These individuals show that HDAC4 haploinsufficiency is not sufficient to produce intellectual disability or the full craniofacial phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Although two patients had some skeletal findings, the deletion region did not contain HDAC4 gene in one of the patients.
evidence.explanation: Skeletal findings in a deletion not containing HDAC4 argue against attributing every skeletal manifestation to that gene.

steps/2.description: HDAC4 loss of function is associated particularly with type E brachydactyly; its contribution to neurobehavioral findings remains uncertain. Human data show incomplete penetrance, normal intelligence in some individuals with HDAC4 haploinsufficiency, and skeletal or cognitive findings in some 2q37 deletions that do not include HDAC4. HDAC4 is therefore modeled as a partial contributor, not the sole initiating mechanism for the deletion syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Reportedly, Hdac4(-/-) mice have severe bone malformations resulting from premature ossification of developing bones.
evidence.explanation: The mouse model supports an ossification mechanism but differs from the heterozygous human dosage state.

steps/3.description: Altered skeletal development is associated with type E brachydactyly and short stature. Hdac4-null mouse evidence suggests premature ossification, but a homozygous-null animal is not a dosage-equivalent model of the human heterozygous deletion.

evidence.snippet: there is a high degree of variability in the presence of some of the features that are considered the most characteristic of the syndrome
evidence.explanation: This supports a variably expressed clinical branch rather than a deterministic phenotype chain.

evidence.snippet: Other findings include seizures (20%-35%), congenital heart disease, CNS abnormalities (hydrocephalus, dilated ventricles), umbilical/inguinal hernia, tracheomalacia, situs abnormalities, gastrointestinal abnormalities, and renal malformations.
evidence.explanation: The retired chapter provides historical clinical evidence for the broad congenital and neurologic spectrum; current frequencies are not inferred from it except where explicitly stated.

steps/4.description: Breakpoint-dependent multigene dosage loss is associated with variable developmental delay, intellectual disability, autistic or other behavioral features, hypotonia, seizures, growth differences, and congenital organ anomalies. Specific gene-to-phenotype routes remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: the disease-related HDAC4 deletion resulted in displaced inter-chromosomal arrangements and altered interactions between the deletion-affected chromosome 2 and chromosome 12 and/or 17
evidence.explanation: This directly supports altered nuclear architecture in the studied patient-derived cells without establishing a phenotype-level causal edge.

steps/5.description: Mesenchymal stem cells and derived cells from members of one family with an inherited 2q37 deletion showed altered positions and interactions of chromosome territories. This is a patient-derived cellular observation; its contribution to particular clinical features is unknown.

evidence.snippet: any increased risk for developing Wilms' tumor likely correlates with deletions encompassing 2q37.1.
evidence.explanation: The study supports a cautious, breakpoint-specific association rather than a syndrome-wide tumor-risk estimate.

steps/6.description: A small number of constitutional 2q37 deletion and Wilms-tumor co-occurrences, together with tumor loss-of-heterozygosity data, suggest a possible susceptibility locus in 2q37.1. The magnitude of constitutional risk and the value of surveillance are not established.

evidence.snippet: overweight and obesity (34%), cognitive-behavioral issues (79%), dysmorphic craniofacial features (86%), and type E brachydactyly (48%).
evidence.explanation: The 86% estimate supports the VERY_FREQUENT band.

steps/7.description: Dysmorphic craniofacial features were reported in 86% of the 103 literature-review cases, although the specific gestalt is variable.

evidence.snippet: overweight and obesity (34%), cognitive-behavioral issues (79%), dysmorphic craniofacial features (86%), and type E brachydactyly (48%).
evidence.explanation: The composite 79% estimate supports the FREQUENT band.

steps/8.description: A combined category of cognitive and behavioral findings was present in 79% of the 103 literature-review cases. This composite does not establish separate frequencies for intellectual disability, developmental delay, autism, or any individual behavioral diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: overweight and obesity (34%), cognitive-behavioral issues (79%), dysmorphic craniofacial features (86%), and type E brachydactyly (48%).
evidence.explanation: The 48% estimate supports the FREQUENT band.

steps/9.description: Type E brachydactyly is characteristic but incompletely penetrant; it was reported in 48% of the 103 literature-review cases.

evidence.snippet: overweight and obesity (34%), cognitive-behavioral issues (79%), dysmorphic craniofacial features (86%), and type E brachydactyly (48%).
evidence.explanation: The 34% estimate supports the FREQUENT band.

steps/10.description: Overweight or obesity was reported in 34% of the 103 literature-review cases and is incompletely penetrant.

evidence.snippet: 2q37 microdeletion syndrome is characterized by mild-moderate developmental delay/intellectual disability
evidence.explanation: The historical source supports the association but not a current, phenotype-specific frequency.

steps/11.description: Developmental delay is a recurrent feature, but the available composite estimates do not support a separate frequency band.

evidence.snippet: However, all of the patients had intellectual disability, especially with a cheerful mood.
evidence.explanation: The three-person series supports intellectual disability as an associated phenotype but is too small for a syndrome-wide frequency.

evidence.snippet: Presented here are three individuals with haploinsufficiency of HDAC4 who have brachydactyly type E, non-dysmorphic facial features, and normal intelligence.
evidence.explanation: This limiting evidence supports variable expression.

steps/12.description: Intellectual disability is variable, and normal intelligence has been reported in some individuals with HDAC4 haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: Chromosome 2q37 deletion syndrome is a rare chromosomal disorder which is characterized by mild-moderate intellectual disability, brachymetaphalangy of digits 3-5, short stature, obesity, hypotonia and characteristic facial appearance.
evidence.explanation: The clinical paper identifies short stature as part of the spectrum.

steps/13.description: Short stature is a recurrent but not quantitatively established feature.

evidence.snippet: the most commonly described hallmark features of the 2q37 deletion syndrome include brachydactyly type E, developmental delay, obesity, autistic features, and craniofacial or skeletal dysmorphism
evidence.explanation: This supports the association but does not supply a separate autism frequency.

steps/14.description: Autism-spectrum features occur in a subset of affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: Chromosome 2q37 deletion syndrome is a rare chromosomal disorder which is characterized by mild-moderate intellectual disability, brachymetaphalangy of digits 3-5, short stature, obesity, hypotonia and characteristic facial appearance.
evidence.explanation: This supports hypotonia without establishing a frequency.

steps/15.description: Hypotonia is part of the reported clinical spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Other findings include seizures (20%-35%), congenital heart disease
evidence.explanation: The historical range supports occurrence but not one repository frequency band.

steps/16.description: Seizures occur in a subset. The historical 20%-35% range crosses repository frequency-band boundaries, so no categorical frequency is assigned.

evidence.snippet: Other findings include seizures (20%-35%), congenital heart disease
evidence.explanation: The historical source supports association without a frequency.

steps/18.description: Hydrocephalus or ventricular enlargement has been reported.

evidence.snippet: gastrointestinal abnormalities, and renal malformations.

steps/19.description: Renal and other genitourinary malformations are variably reported.

evidence.snippet: umbilical/inguinal hernia, tracheomalacia, situs abnormalities, gastrointestinal abnormalities, and renal malformations.
evidence.explanation: The historical source supports the reported gastrointestinal spectrum.

steps/20.description: Gastrointestinal and abdominal-wall anomalies are variably reported.

evidence.snippet: Cooccurrence of Wilms' tumor with 2q37 deletion syndrome, an uncommon constitutional chromosome abnormality, has been reported previously in three children.
evidence.explanation: This documents rare co-occurrence but does not establish penetrance or a categorical frequency.

steps/21.description: Wilms tumor has co-occurred with constitutional 2q37 deletion, especially when 2q37.1 is included, but syndrome-wide penetrance is unknown.

edges/1.description: A deletion that includes HDAC4 directly reduces its dosage, but not every 2q37 deletion includes HDAC4 and HDAC4 loss is not sufficient to explain the full phenotype.

edges/2.description: Variable deleted gene content produces incompletely penetrant neurodevelopmental, growth, and organ-development findings.

edges/3.description: One patient-derived cellular study found altered chromosome-territory interactions associated with an inherited 2q37 deletion.

edges/4.description: When the deletion extends into 2q37.1, a possible breakpoint-specific Wilms-tumor association has been reported.

edges/5.description: HDAC4 dosage loss may alter skeletal development and contribute to type E brachydactyly.

edges/6.description: Altered skeletal development produces the characteristic type E brachydactyly.

edges/7.description: Skeletal and broader growth effects may contribute to short stature.

edges/8.description: The deletion is associated with a composite of cognitive and behavioral findings, without a resolved gene-specific route.

edges/9.description: Variable dosage loss can impair early development.

edges/10.description: Variable dosage loss can produce intellectual disability.

edges/11.description: Autism-spectrum features occur in a subset of affected individuals.

edges/12.description: Hypotonia contributes to early motor delay in some individuals.

edges/13.description: Seizures occur in a subset of affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: Chromosome analysis confirms the diagnosis of 2q37 deletion syndrome in 80%-85% of affected individuals.
evidence.explanation: The historical source supports the defining chromosomal lesion while reflecting older testing technology.

evidence.snippet: more detailed molecular diagnoses are possible than in years past, enabling refined characterization of the genotype-phenotype correlation for subjects with 2q37 deletions.
evidence.explanation: This supports breakpoint-aware interpretation of the deletion.

genes/0.notes: The defining event is a terminal or interstitial deletion involving 2q37. Breakpoint and gene-content interpretation should remain explicit because the clinical phenotype is variably expressed.

evidence.explanation: This supports a gene-level contribution to an overlapping phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Presented here are three individuals with haploinsufficiency of HDAC4 who have brachydactyly type E, non-dysmorphic facial features, and normal intelligence.
evidence.explanation: This establishes incomplete penetrance for nonskeletal features.

genes/1.notes: HDAC4 loss is associated with an overlapping brachydactyly phenotype, but incomplete penetrance and findings outside HDAC4-containing intervals make it insufficient as a complete explanation of 2q37 microdeletion syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Multidisciplinary care by specialists in the following fields is often required: clinical genetics, speech pathology, occupational and physical therapy, child development, neurology, cardiology, gastroenterology, nutrition/feeding, ophthalmology, and audiology.
evidence.explanation: The retired chapter supports multidisciplinary, feature-directed care but not contemporary syndrome-specific efficacy claims.

treatments/0.description: Management is feature-directed and coordinated across developmental, neurologic, cardiac, gastrointestinal, nutritional, vision, hearing, and genetics services according to the individual's findings. The cited syndrome-specific management source is retired and is retained as historical guidance rather than current evidence for fixed protocols.

evidence.snippet: Infants benefit from enrollment in an early-intervention program; most school-age children benefit from an individualized educational program (IEP).
evidence.explanation: This provides historical syndrome-specific support for developmental and educational services.

treatments/1.description: Early developmental services and individualized educational support can be used for developmental, communication, motor, and learning needs.

evidence.snippet: The risk to sibs of a proband depends on the chromosome findings in the parents
evidence.explanation: This supports family-specific recurrence counseling.

treatments/2.description: Genetic counseling integrates the proband's deletion boundaries and parental chromosome results when estimating recurrence risk.

evidence.snippet: any increased risk for developing Wilms' tumor likely correlates with deletions encompassing 2q37.1.
evidence.explanation: The association is limited to a possible 2q37.1-containing subgroup and does not define a screening protocol.

evidence.snippet: For young children with a deletion that includes 2q37.1, screening for Wilms tumor can be considered.
evidence.explanation: The retired source supports consideration, not a universal recommendation; current expert guidance remains needed.

treatments/3.description: For a young child whose deletion encompasses 2q37.1, clinical genetics and pediatric oncology input can be used to decide whether renal ultrasound surveillance is appropriate. Available evidence is breakpoint-specific and does not establish a universal schedule or syndrome-wide recommendation.

evidence.snippet: No new carious lesions have developed during this period and notable improvement in anterior alignment has been achieved.
evidence.explanation: This single case supports feasibility of individualized long-term dental and orthodontic care, not general efficacy.

treatments/4.description: Dental assessment, preventive care, and orthodontic planning can be individualized. Evidence is limited to a single long-term case and does not establish a syndrome-wide dental protocol.

evidence.snippet: This is in contradistinction to previous reports that haploinsufficiency of HDAC4 is sufficient to cause BDMR.
evidence.explanation: This directly identifies the disputed sufficiency claim.

hypotheses/0.description: A plasma-cell clone produces an amyloidogenic monoclonal light chain that misfolds, forms beta-sheet-rich oligomers and fibrils, deposits in the extracellular matrix of multiple organs, and causes organ-specific dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we report that amyloidogenic light chain (AL-LC) proteins provoke oxidative stress, cellular dysfunction, and apoptosis in isolated adult cardiomyocytes through activation of p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK).
evidence.explanation: Isolated adult cardiomyocytes provide direct experimental support for a soluble-light-chain injury branch independent of extracellular fibril burden.

hypotheses/1.description: Soluble or prefibrillar amyloidogenic light chains exert direct cardiac proteotoxicity superimposed on structural injury from deposited fibrils, activating oxidative stress and non-canonical p38alpha MAPK signaling in cardiomyocytes and promoting contractile dysfunction and apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: However, effective therapies for patients with advanced cardiac involvement are an unmet need.
evidence.explanation: The review explicitly identifies the advanced-cardiac treatment gap.

evidence.snippet: The primary purpose of this study is to determine whether CAEL-101, a monoclonal antibody that removes AL amyloid deposits from tissues and organs, improves overall survival, reduces cardiovascular related hospitalizations and it is safe and well tolerated in patients with stage IIIa AL amyloidosis.
evidence.explanation: The registry describes an ongoing investigational deposit-directed strategy but does not establish benefit.

evidence.snippet: A Phase 3 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of birtamimab plus standard of care compared to placebo plus standard of care in Mayo Stage IV patients with AL amyloidosis.
evidence.explanation: The registry cache supports the confirmatory trial design; its terminated status was independently verified and prevents portraying the agent as established.

open_questions/0.rationale: Advanced cardiac disease remains a major unmet need. CAEL-101 phase III programs remain active but closed to new enrollment, while the confirmatory birtamimab phase III trial was terminated after missing its primary endpoint; no fibril-clearing strategy should therefore be represented as established.

evidence.snippet: KIF7, the human ortholog of Drosophila Costal2, is a key component of the Hedgehog signaling pathway
evidence.explanation: Identifies KIF7 as a core Hedgehog pathway component (Costal2 ortholog), establishing the molecular basis of the ACLS mechanism.

evidence.snippet: we show deregulation of most GLI transcription factor targets and impaired GLI3 processing in tissues from individuals with KIF7 mutations
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the downstream molecular consequence of KIF7 loss in patient tissues: deregulated GLI targets and impaired GLI3 processing.

evidence.snippet: Our data show the role of KIF7 in human primary cilia, especially in the Hedgehog pathway through the regulation of GLI targets, and expand the clinical spectrum of ciliopathies
evidence.explanation: Places ACLS within the primary-cilium Hedgehog-signaling ciliopathy spectrum, supporting conformance to the ciliopathy module Hedgehog node.

evidence.snippet: In vertebrates, Hedgehog signaling requires the primary cilium, and KIF7 and Gli transcription factors accumulate at the cilium tip in response to Hedgehog activation
evidence.explanation: Cell-based evidence that KIF7 is a cilium-tip Hedgehog regulator whose ciliary accumulation is coupled to pathway activation.

evidence.snippet: we show that the immotile behavior of KIF7 is required to prevent ciliary localization of Gli transcription factors in the absence of Hedgehog signaling
evidence.explanation: Mechanistic detail that KIF7 restrains GLI in the unstimulated state, explaining how loss of function deregulates GLI output.

steps/1.description: KIF7, the human ortholog of Drosophila Costal2, is an immotile kinesin-4 protein that localizes to the tip of the primary cilium, where it organizes the cilium-tip compartment and regulates the GLI transcription factors of the Hedgehog pathway. In the absence of Hedgehog ligand KIF7 promotes processing of GLI3 into its transcriptional repressor form; upon pathway activation KIF7 and GLI accumulate at the cilium tip. Pathogenic KIF7 dysfunction deregulates GLI target genes and impairs GLI3 processing, disrupting the tightly dosed Hedgehog output required for midline brain, limb, and craniofacial patterning.

evidence.snippet: decreased GLI3R signaling is fully responsible for the ACLS features in these mice, as all phenotypes are rescued by increasing GLI3R activity.
evidence.explanation: Genetic rescue in the mouse model places reduced GLI3-repressor activity downstream of Kif7 depletion.

evidence.snippet: increased FGF8 signaling is responsible in part for CC defects associated to KIF7 depletion, as modulating FGF8 signaling rescued CC formation anteriorly in Kif7-/- mice.
evidence.explanation: Functional rescue supports increased FGF8 signaling as a partial mediator of the modeled callosal defect.

steps/2.description: KIF7 depletion lowers GLI3-repressor signaling and overactivates SHH target genes. In the Kif7-null model, restoring GLI3-repressor activity rescues the modeled ACLS features, while increased FGF8 signaling contributes specifically to anterior corpus-callosum defects.

evidence.snippet: Acrocallosal syndrome (ACLS) is a rare recessive disorder characterised by corpus callosum agenesis or hypoplasia, craniofacial dysmorphism, duplication of the hallux, postaxial polydactyly, and severe mental retardation
evidence.explanation: Establishes corpus callosum agenesis/hypoplasia as a defining CNS feature of ACLS.

evidence.snippet: vermis dysgenesis with brainstem anomalies (molar tooth sign), strongly indicated the diagnosis
evidence.explanation: Documents cerebellar vermis dysgenesis and the molar tooth sign as diagnostically informative CNS malformations in ACLS.

steps/3.description: Impaired cilium-dependent Hedgehog signaling during neurodevelopment produces the hallmark CNS malformations of ACLS: agenesis or hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and cerebellar vermis dysgenesis. In a subset of patients the cerebellar/brainstem malformation is severe enough to generate the molar tooth sign on MRI, overlapping with Joubert syndrome and reflecting the shared ciliary Hedgehog mechanism.

evidence.snippet: CC agenesis in these mice is associated with specific patterning defects of the cortical septum boundary leading to altered distribution of guidepost cells required to guide the callosal axons through the midline.
evidence.explanation: Defines the cortical-midline cellular mechanism and its role in callosal axon guidance.

steps/4.description: In the Kif7-null model, cortical septum-boundary patterning is abnormal and guidepost cells required for callosal axons to cross the midline are redistributed. This provides an experimentally resolved route to callosal agenesis; its detailed cellular sequence remains model-organism evidence.

evidence.snippet: overlapping features that include polydactyly, brain abnormalities and cleft palate
evidence.explanation: Original KIF7 report supports limb and craniofacial malformations as part of the KIF7 ciliopathy spectrum.

evidence.snippet: characterized by postaxial and/or preaxial polydactyly, cutaneous syndactyly, macrocephaly, widely spaced eyes, absence or hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, and intellectual disability
evidence.explanation: Review evidence connects KIF7-associated ACLS to polydactyly, syndactyly, macrocephaly, and hypertelorism.

steps/5.description: KIF7-dependent Hedgehog/GLI3 signaling is required for dosed limb and craniofacial patterning. Deregulated GLI output produces polydactyly, hallux duplication, syndactyly, cleft palate, and the characteristic macrocephalic craniofacial appearance.

evidence.snippet: Acrocallosal syndrome (ACLS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by agenesis of the corpus callosum
evidence.explanation: Corpus callosum agenesis is the eponymous, defining CNS malformation of ACLS.

steps/6.description: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum is a cardinal ACLS feature and gives the syndrome its name; partial hypoplasia is represented separately.

evidence.snippet: Acrocallosal syndrome (ACLS) is a rare recessive disorder characterised by corpus callosum agenesis or hypoplasia
evidence.explanation: Explicitly documents hypoplasia as part of the callosal phenotype rather than collapsing all cases into complete agenesis.

steps/7.description: Partial underdevelopment of the corpus callosum is an alternative to complete agenesis within the KIF7-related ACLS spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Acrocallosal syndrome is a multiple congenital anomaly disorder characterized by postaxial and/or preaxial polydactyly
evidence.explanation: Postaxial polydactyly is a cardinal limb malformation of ACLS.

steps/8.description: Postaxial polydactyly of the hands is one of the two cardinal limb features of ACLS, reflecting deregulated Hedgehog/GLI3 anterior-posterior limb patterning.

evidence.snippet: postaxial polydactyly of the hands as well as preaxial polydactyly of the feet
evidence.explanation: Preaxial polydactyly of the feet is a recognized cardinal limb feature of ACLS.

steps/9.description: Preaxial polydactyly of the feet, frequently manifesting as duplication of the hallux, is characteristic of ACLS.

steps/10.description: Duplication of the hallux (great toe) is a distinctive preaxial digital malformation in ACLS.

evidence.snippet: Facial dysmorphism with hypertelorism and prominent forehead in all the cases
evidence.explanation: Prominent forehead was present in all cases of this ACLS series, supporting VERY_FREQUENT classification.

steps/13.description: A prominent (bossed) forehead is a consistent craniofacial feature of ACLS.

steps/17.description: Cerebellar vermis dysgenesis/hypoplasia, sometimes severe enough to produce the molar tooth sign, occurs in ACLS and overlaps with Joubert syndrome.

evidence.snippet: They present with features like molar tooth sign and hyperventilation that are not very typical in ACLS, but do occur in other ciliopathies
evidence.explanation: The molar tooth sign is described as "not very typical" in ACLS, supporting its presence in a variable subset without assigning a frequency from qualitative wording.

steps/18.description: The molar tooth sign on MRI (deepened interpeduncular fossa with elongated, thickened superior cerebellar peduncles) can occur in ACLS, reflecting the shared ciliary Hedgehog mechanism with Joubert syndrome.

evidence.snippet: showed partial callosal agenesis, pachygyria, ventriculomegaly, agenesis of cerebellar vermis and Dandy–Walker malformation.
evidence.explanation: A KIF7-confirmed infant had Dandy-Walker malformation on MRI, supporting inclusion without assigning a population frequency.

steps/20.description: Cleft palate occurs in a subset of ACLS cases and is also a feature of the allelic hydrolethalus syndrome, reflecting shared deregulation of midline craniofacial Hedgehog patterning.

evidence.snippet: we report mutations in KIF7 in individuals with hydrolethalus and acrocallosal syndromes, two multiple malformation disorders with overlapping features that include polydactyly, brain abnormalities and cleft palate
evidence.explanation: Original report identifying KIF7 as the causative gene for both ACLS and the allelic hydrolethalus syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Seven mutations were identified at the KIF7 locus in these five cases, six of which are novel
evidence.explanation: Mutation series confirming KIF7 as the recurrent disease locus and expanding the allelic spectrum of ACLS.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the KIF7 gene, encoding a molecule within the Sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway, have been identified as causative for ACLS but also for the fatal hydrolethalus syndrome and some cases of Joubert syndrome
evidence.explanation: Confirms KIF7 causation of ACLS and the allelic relationship with hydrolethalus and Joubert syndromes.

evidence.snippet: We present two children who both had two missense mutations in the Kinesin Family Member 7 (KIF7) gene.
evidence.explanation: Supports only that biallelic missense substitutions have been reported; the paper itself was tentative and does not establish every reported missense allele as pathogenic.

genes/0.notes: Biallelic pathogenic variants in KIF7 (15q26.1) cause the autosomal recessive form modeled here. Truncating and splice-disrupting alleles are well established; biallelic missense substitutions have also been reported, but individual missense findings require variant-level interpretation. Allelic KIF7 disease spans the more severe hydrolethalus syndrome 2 and Joubert-spectrum presentations. Rare de novo GLI3-related acrocallosal phenocopies are handled as a differential, not as a second causal gene in this KIF7-scoped entry.

evidence.snippet: Treatment includes physical therapy in infancy which may assist in the development of motor skills and muscle tone.
evidence.explanation: Supports early physical therapy for hypotonia and motor delay.

evidence.snippet: Antiepileptic therapy for seizure disorder and antihypertensives for renoparenchymal hypertension are to be given.
evidence.explanation: Supports symptom-directed antiseizure treatment when seizures occur.

evidence.snippet: At present, the child is referred to a neurodevelopment specialist, for neurodevelopment assessment and occupational therapist for infant stimulation program.
evidence.explanation: A genetically confirmed case documents specialist developmental follow-up and occupational-therapy referral.

treatments/0.description: Management is symptom-directed and multidisciplinary. Early physical, occupational, developmental, and communication support addresses hypotonia and developmental disability; seizures are treated with standard antiseizure therapy when present. Available evidence is case-report and clinical-review level rather than ACLS-specific comparative trials.

evidence.snippet: Surgery to remove extra fingers and toes and release fused fingers may improve movement and grasp, may assist in walking and the comfort of footwear.
evidence.explanation: Supports symptom-directed surgery for polydactyly and syndactyly while making no disease-modifying claim.

evidence.snippet: She underwent Nissen fundoplication at 4 months of age, cleft lip repair at 6 months age and cleft palate repair at 18 months of age using the same technique.
evidence.explanation: A KIF7-confirmed case documents actual surgical repair of associated structural manifestations, including cleft palate.

treatments/1.description: Individually indicated surgery may remove functionally limiting extra digits, release syndactyly, or repair orofacial and other structural malformations. These procedures treat local manifestations rather than the underlying ciliary signaling defect.

evidence.snippet: As the mode of inheritance of ACLS is autosomal recessive, the risk of recurrence is 25%. Genetic counselling is of prime importance
evidence.explanation: Directly supports recurrence-risk counseling for the autosomal recessive KIF7 form.

evidence.snippet: Polydactyly, and central nervous system malformations can be detected by ultrasonography in the second trimester, but due to variability of presentation, prenatal diagnosis may not always be possible.
evidence.explanation: Supports balanced counseling about prenatal ultrasound capabilities and limits.

treatments/2.description: When biallelic KIF7 disease is confirmed, parents should be counseled about autosomal recessive inheritance and a 25% recurrence risk in each pregnancy. Prenatal ultrasound can detect polydactyly and major CNS malformations but cannot exclude disease because presentation is variable. This recurrence statement does not apply to a rare de novo GLI3 phenocopy.

evidence.snippet: Optical coherence tomography angiography illustrated a flow void in the deep retinal capillary plexus associated with the AMN lesion.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates deep capillary plexus flow deficit at the site of the AMN lesion via OCT angiography.

evidence.snippet: All five eyes had reduced DCP flow signal, along with normal SCP, MCP, and choriocapillaris flow signal in the area of the lesion
evidence.explanation: Projection-resolved OCTA localizes the AMN flow deficit specifically to the deep capillary plexus, distinguishing it from the more superficial plexus involvement seen in paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM).

steps/0.description: In predisposed individuals, transient microvascular occlusion/ischemia develops in the deep capillary plexus (DCP) of the retina, the vascular bed supplying the outer plexiform and outer nuclear layers. OCT angiography directly demonstrates a flow void in the DCP co-localized with the acute lesion, with partial recovery of flow signal on follow-up in most cases.

evidence.snippet: Two patients were seen within the first 1 to 2 days of symptoms, and both showed outer nuclear and outer plexiform layer hyperreflectivity.
evidence.explanation: Establishes acute OPL/ONL hyperreflectivity as the earliest OCT finding, with lesion enlargement over the following week.

evidence.snippet: hyperreflective lesions at the level of the outer plexiform layer (OPL) and outer nuclear layer (ONL) and disruption of the ellipsoid zone (EZ) on spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) B-scans
evidence.explanation: Confirms the OPL/ONL hyperreflectivity and ellipsoid zone disruption pattern as the characteristic acute OCT signature of AMN.

steps/1.description: Deep capillary plexus ischemia infarcts the outer plexiform layer (OPL) and outer nuclear layer (ONL), producing acute hyperreflectivity at the OPL/ONL junction on OCT that enlarges over the first week, with disruption of the ellipsoid zone and outer segment/RPE junction. The lesion is best visualized as a dark area on near-infrared reflectance imaging.

evidence.snippet: Thinning of the outer nuclear layer persisted in all patients with lesions >100 μm width, and in one patient this thinning worsened over the course of follow-up
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the size-dependent persistence of ONL thinning and its correlation with long-term functional (visual field) deficits.

evidence.snippet: all patients achieved a BCVA of 20/40 or better, but 9 patients (81.8%) continued to experience persistent scotomas
evidence.explanation: Shows that visual acuity typically recovers while paracentral scotomas frequently persist, consistent with the structural ONL thinning outcome.

steps/2.description: Lesions wider than 100 micrometers develop persistent thinning of the outer nuclear layer that correlates with long-term visual field deficits (paracentral scotomas). Visual acuity often recovers within weeks, but scotomas frequently persist for months or longer.

evidence.snippet: Although the pathogenesis of acute macular neuroretinopathy is complex, recent research suggests a microvascular etiology.
evidence.explanation: Underscores that despite advances in understanding AMN's microvascular etiology, no proven pharmacologic treatment has emerged; management remains observational.

treatments/0.description: No pharmacologic or interventional treatment has proven effective for AMN; management consists of observation and monitoring, since surgery and pharmacotherapy have no established role in this ischemic outer retinal condition.

evidence.snippet: Optical coherence tomography angiography illustrated a flow void in the deep retinal capillary plexus associated with the AMN lesion.
evidence.explanation: Direct OCTA evidence for the deep capillary plexus ischemia model.

hypotheses/0.description: Ischemia/microvascular occlusion of the retinal deep capillary plexus infarcts the outer plexiform and outer nuclear layers, producing the characteristic acute OCT hyperreflectivity and long-term photoreceptor layer thinning. This is the predominant model in the current literature, supported by OCT angiography studies directly localizing the flow deficit to the deep capillary plexus.

evidence.snippet: Our data suggests that a perfusion deficit in the choroidal layers is responsible for AMN rather than in the DCP, which is the predominant hypothesis in current literature.
evidence.explanation: Primary evidence for the emerging choriocapillaris/choroidal perfusion-deficit alternative to the canonical DCP-ischemia model.

hypotheses/1.description: An alternative hypothesis proposes that the primary perfusion deficit in AMN lies in the choriocapillaris and choroid rather than the deep capillary plexus, based on quantitative OCTA vessel-area-density analysis finding no retinal-layer flow differences but significantly reduced choriocapillaris and choroidal density in COVID-19-associated AMN cases.

evidence.snippet: neutrophils are responsible for the initiation and development of inflammation through the release of a wide variety of granular enzymes and antimicrobial proteins
evidence.explanation: Neutrophil activation is identified as a fundamental initiating event in AOSD inflammation.

steps/0.description: Neutrophil activation is a fundamental early innate-immune event in AOSD. Activated neutrophils release granular enzymes and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) that activate macrophages and, through NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and caspase-1, drive IL-1beta and IL-18 production, feeding the macrophage-centered cytokine cascade.

evidence.snippet: Pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6 and IL-18 play a fundamental role in disease onset and progression.
evidence.explanation: Identifies IL-1, IL-6, and IL-18 as the pivotal cytokines driving AOSD.

steps/1.description: Innate immune and inflammasome activation amplifies pro-inflammatory cytokines, principally interleukin-1 (IL-1), IL-6, and IL-18, which are implicated in disease onset and progression.

evidence.snippet: The central role of macrophage activation, which results in T helper 1 (Th1) cell cytokine activation, is well established.
evidence.explanation: Establishes macrophage activation as the central initiating immunologic event of AOSD.

steps/2.description: Dysregulated innate immunity centers on activation of macrophages, the established central immunologic event that initiates the AOSD inflammatory cascade.

evidence.snippet: The central role of macrophage activation, which results in T helper 1 (Th1) cell cytokine activation, is well established.
evidence.explanation: Identifies Th1 cell cytokine activation as the consequence of macrophage activation.

steps/3.description: Macrophage activation is reported to produce a T helper 1 (Th1) cytokine response. The current evidence establishes this immune response but does not establish the previous downstream arrow from Th1 cells to the IL-1/IL-6/IL-18 amplification node.

evidence.snippet: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a multisystemic complex disorder clinically characterised by episodes of spiking fever, evanescent rash, polyarthritis or diffuse arthralgias; multiorgan involvement may develop according to the hyper-inflammatory extent.

evidence.snippet: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology, characterized by a clinical triad of high spiking fever, arthralgia (± arthritis), and evanescent skin rash.
evidence.explanation: An evanescent skin rash is one of the three defining features of the AOSD triad.

steps/6.description: A characteristic transient, salmon-colored (pink) maculopapular rash that typically appears with fever spikes and fades as the fever subsides.

evidence.snippet: sore throat (50%, n=15), hepatomegaly (40%, n=12), splenomegaly (23.3%, n=7)
evidence.explanation: Sore throat occurred in 50% of a single-center AOSD cohort.

steps/7.description: Sore throat (nonsuppurative pharyngitis) is a common early symptom and is included as a criterion in some classification systems.

evidence.snippet: sore throat (50%, n=15), hepatomegaly (40%, n=12), splenomegaly (23.3%, n=7)
evidence.explanation: Hepatomegaly occurred in 40% of a single-center AOSD cohort.

steps/8.description: Hepatic enlargement reflects reticuloendothelial/multiorgan inflammatory involvement; transaminitis frequently accompanies it.

evidence.snippet: sore throat (50%, n=15), hepatomegaly (40%, n=12), splenomegaly (23.3%, n=7)
evidence.explanation: Splenomegaly occurred in ~23% of a single-center AOSD cohort.

steps/9.description: Splenic enlargement is part of the reticuloendothelial involvement of AOSD.

evidence.snippet: skin rash (36.6%, n=11) and pericarditis (20%, n=6)
evidence.explanation: Pericarditis (serositis) occurred in 20% of a single-center AOSD cohort.

steps/10.description: Serositis, most often pericarditis, is the commonest cardiac manifestation of AOSD.

evidence.snippet: macrophage activation syndrome - reported in as high as 23% of AOSD patients and considered to be the most severe complication characterized by a high mortality rate
evidence.explanation: MAS occurs in up to ~23% of AOSD patients and is the most severe, high-mortality complication.

steps/11.description: Macrophage activation syndrome (secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) is the most severe complication of AOSD, marked by uncontrolled macrophage/T-cell activation, hemophagocytosis, and high mortality.

evidence.snippet: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology, characterized by a clinical triad of high spiking fever, arthralgia (± arthritis), and evanescent skin rash.
evidence.explanation: Arthralgia with or without arthritis is one of the three defining features of the AOSD triad.

steps/12.description: Joint involvement ranges from diffuse arthralgias to polyarthritis and is part of the defining clinical triad.

evidence.snippet: myalgia (96.6%, n=29)
evidence.explanation: Myalgia was present in 96.6% of a single-center AOSD cohort, among the most frequent manifestations.

steps/13.description: Diffuse muscle pain is a very common systemic symptom, frequently accompanying the febrile episodes.

evidence.snippet: more than 80% of patients may develop neutrophilic leucocytosis
evidence.explanation: More than 80% of patients develop neutrophilic leukocytosis during Still's disease flares.

evidence.snippet: leukocytosis (100%, n=30)
evidence.explanation: Leukocytosis was present in 100% of a single-center AOSD cohort.

steps/14.description: Marked neutrophil-predominant leukocytosis is a hallmark laboratory feature of active AOSD, developing in the majority of patients during febrile flares.

evidence.snippet: the release of NETs plays a key role in activating macrophages
evidence.explanation: NET release activates macrophages, linking neutrophil activation to the macrophage-centered cascade.

edges/0.description: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) activate macrophages.

evidence.snippet: the activation of NLRP3 stimulates the production of IL-1β and IL-18
evidence.explanation: NLRP3 inflammasome activation stimulates IL-1beta and IL-18 production, feeding the pro-inflammatory cytokine amplification node.

edges/1.description: NLRP3 inflammasome activation stimulates IL-1beta and IL-18 production.

evidence.snippet: During Still’s disease flares, more than 80% of patients may develop neutrophilic leucocytosis
evidence.explanation: The review documents neutrophilic leukocytosis during flares but does not establish that neutrophil activation causes the count increase.

edges/2.description: Neutrophil activation accompanies neutrophil-predominant leukocytosis during Still disease flares; the edge is typed UNKNOWN because the cited clinical evidence does not resolve whether activation drives cell-number expansion or merely co-occurs with it.

evidence.snippet: The central role of macrophage activation, which results in T helper 1 (Th1) cell cytokine activation, is well established.
evidence.explanation: Macrophage activation is stated to result in Th1 cell cytokine activation.

edges/3.description: Macrophage activation drives a T helper 1 (Th1) cell cytokine response.

evidence.snippet: Pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6 and IL-18 play a fundamental role in disease onset and progression.
evidence.explanation: The review supports a disease-driving role for the cytokine axis but does not resolve every intermediate between cytokine elevation and multiorgan manifestations.

edges/4.description: Cytokine amplification contributes to the systemic hyperinflammatory state; organ-level intermediates are not represented in this compact pathograph.

evidence.snippet: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a multisystemic complex disorder clinically characterised by episodes of spiking fever, evanescent rash, polyarthritis or diffuse arthralgias; multiorgan involvement may develop according to the hyper-inflammatory extent.
evidence.explanation: The review co-describes spiking fever and hyperinflammatory extent but does not resolve the full causal route.

edges/5.description: Spiking fever is a defining manifestation of the systemic inflammatory state; intervening thermoregulatory mechanisms are not modeled.

edges/6.description: Evanescent rash is a defining manifestation of systemic inflammation; its intervening skin-level mechanisms are not modeled.

edges/7.description: Arthralgia and arthritis are defining manifestations of the systemic inflammatory state; synovial intermediates are not modeled.

evidence.explanation: A single-center cohort supports the clinical association; causal directness is intentionally unresolved.

edges/11.description: Pericarditis is a reported systemic manifestation, but the cited cohort does not establish the organ-specific causal route.
